origin.discovery_context: Found while verifying the three MT-017 final-hardening fixes on 2026-07-30. Deferred into its own MT per the Operator rule that an unexpected gap not belonging to the current MT is carried into a future MT in the same work packet so it is not lost.

scope.summary: Close the WP-1 operator-surface gaps: make the WP-1 Orchestration Console swarm-dispatchable, and expose the missing WP-1 controls (cloud consent/export posture, swarm concurrency) in Options/Settings.
scope.root_cause: A 2026-07-30 audit of the native shell found the menu bar essentially complete - a MODELS menu exists (top_menu_bar.rs, MENU_DEFINITIONS ~:214-222) and all three WP-1 panes are reachable and Argus-proven: Wp1OrchestrationConsole via MODELS > Open Console (:716-724, proof tests/test_wp1_console_stream_pane_argus.rs:65-93), OperatorChatLaunch (:680-688), SwarmLaneDiagnostics (:707-715). TWO REAL GAPS REMAIN. (1) SWARM_ACCESSIBLE_ACTIONS (top_menu_bar.rs:274-288) lists 13 keys and OMITS menu.models.wp1-orchestration-console, so a swarm agent cannot dispatch the WP-1 console the way it can the other four MODELS leaves; the count is pinned by assert_eq!(len, 13) at :1016-1020. (2) settings_dialog.rs has 9 sections but NO cloud consent / export posture control anywhere (backend types exist at llm/guard.rs:55-195 and migration 0353, but api/mod.rs:350 stubs consent: None and no consent route exists in api/model_access.rs:354-366), and the Swarm section (:1177-1252) contains NO concurrency/lease control - its two interval rows are hardcoded read-only literals (settings.not-wired.swarm-reconcile-interval :1180, settings.not-wired.swarm-resource-poll-interval :1181).
forbidden_paths: adding a settings section BEFORE the Layout section (settings_dialog.rs:1311-1314 is normative: earlier insertion pushes existing sections' widgets out of the coordinate-clickable viewport and regresses their kittest interaction proofs)
granting authority from a UI control - a Settings toggle must never widen consent or access scope
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: menu.models.wp1-orchestration-console is added to SWARM_ACCESSIBLE_ACTIONS and the pinned assert_eq!(len, 13) at top_menu_bar.rs:1016-1020 is updated to 14. A swarm agent can dispatch the WP-1 console through the same path as the other MODELS leaves; prove with an Argus/AccessKit test, not by inspection.

AC-2: Cloud consent / export posture is visible in Settings for each configured provider lane, including the current posture and the denial reason when access is refused, WITHOUT revealing restricted resource metadata (HBR-PRIV-008). If the backend cannot yet supply real posture (api/mod.rs:350 currently stubs consent: None), the UI MUST show an explicit not-wired/unavailable state and MUST NOT fabricate a posture. Decide and record whether wiring the backend consent route belongs here or in a follow-up MT.

AC-3: The Swarm settings section exposes at least one REAL concurrency control bound to actual runtime behaviour (e.g. the coordinator's max_concurrent budget), persisted through workspace settings, or - if the runtime does not yet accept a configured value - the section explicitly states the value is fixed and why, replacing the misleading hardcoded literals.

AC-4: Every new control carries a stable Argus author_id, follows the acknowledge_action_effect ack rule (settings_dialog.rs:1775-1783), and is added to the settings_author_ids_are_stable pin list (:1854-1868).

AC-5: Pre-existing coverage holes closed: the four WP-1 settings author_ids at settings_dialog.rs:120/124/126/128 currently have ZERO test references and are absent from the stability pin list; and tests/test_visual_interaction_proof.rs:902-912 lists only 6 of 9 section ids (omits cloud-models, model-runtime, diagnostics). Add the missing pins/ids.
AC-6: HBR-VIS - every changed surface is proven through headless non-intrusive Argus with before/after observation; no foregrounding, no OS cursor automation.
scope.risk_if_missed: The WP-1 console stays undispatchable by the swarm it exists to observe, and the operator has no surface for cloud consent posture or swarm concurrency - the two controls that decide whether cloud data leaves the machine and how hard the machine is driven.

implementation_notes: Menu leaf convention (top_menu_bar.rs:403 menu_items): self.item(ui, "menu.{menu}.{leaf}", label, shortcut, enabled, MenuBarAction::NavigateToTab("<tab-id>"), action); then add the arm to dispatch_menu_action (app.rs:3754, exhaustive match) and the string->PaneType arm in navigate_to_tab (app.rs:3731-3741).

Settings control convention is 7 steps: author_id const (:99-166) -> search gate + CollapsingHeader + set_author_id_ack_click section tag -> per-widget set_author_id / set_author_id_and_label -> ack INSIDE the guarded changed() block -> new SettingsOutcome variant (:433-485) -> handle in apply_settings_outcome (app.rs:3113-3220) -> persist across 5 coordinated edits in workspace_settings.rs (field :166-183, default :241-257, serialize :213-234, parse :383-451) plus DialogState::draft_settings (settings_dialog.rs:561-588).
The dialog never mutates app state directly (settings_dialog.rs:28-36, :505-519) - it returns a SettingsOutcome.
Settings persist to PostgreSQL via PUT /workspaces/{id}/settings (schema hsk.workspace_settings_state@1); there is no local settings file. BYOK keys deliberately bypass that blob.

risks: Displaying a fabricated consent posture because the backend stubs consent: None
A Settings control that appears to grant or widen consent scope
Leaking restricted resource metadata through a denial reason
Inserting a section before Layout and silently regressing other sections' interaction proofs
minimum_controls: Any unwired value renders as an explicit not-wired state, never as a plausible default
Argus proof shows the rendered posture matches backend authorization state
Denial reasons are asserted to contain no restricted resource identifiers
Existing settings interaction proofs stay green

handshake_compatibility.durable_authority: PostgreSQL workspace settings (hsk.workspace_settings_state@1) + EventLedger; no SQLite
handshake_compatibility.spec_realism_gate: Controls must drive real runtime behaviour and be proven through Argus against the running shell; a rendered widget with no backend effect does not satisfy this MT.
